memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do not move your neighbor's boundary stone set up by your predecessors in the inheritance you receive in the land the Lord your God is giving you to possess. - Deut 19:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God turns from matters of life and death to something that might seem small, a boundary stone. In those days, stones marked the edges of each family's land. To secretly move a boundary stone was to quietly steal from your neighbour, taking what was rightfully theirs while pretending nothing was wrong. God forbids this deceptive theft.

Why does God care about a stone in a field? Because He cares about honesty, fairness, and respecting what belongs to others. This law protected families, especially the weak, from being slowly robbed by greedy or dishonest neighbours. Small acts of dishonesty matter to God, because they reveal the heart and because they wound real people.

This speaks to us today, even without boundary stones. We are tempted in countless small ways to take what is not ours, to shade the truth, to quietly benefit at another's expense, to overlook others' rights when it suits us. God calls His people to a deep integrity that respects others even when no one is watching. The New Testament calls us to do nothing out of selfish ambition, but to value others above ourselves (Phil 2:3-4). Honesty in small things reflects a heart shaped by God. Are there any "boundary stones" in your life, small dishonesties you have been quietly excusing?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tempted toward small dishonesties?
2. How can you better respect what belongs to others?
3. What does integrity "when no one is watching" look like for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me honest even in small things. Help me respect what belongs to others and walk with true integrity. Amen.
